title: Who eats whom: simple food chains
examples: Teacher, where does the energy start in a food chain?
Can you show me an example of a plant eater?
What happens if all the plants disappear?

explain.say: Today we learn about food chains. A food chain shows how energy moves. Energy starts with the sun for life.

draw.text: Who eats whom: simple food chains

explain.say: Now look! Here it is in 3D: a food web. Can you see the sun and the grass? Tap any part, and I will tell you about it.

draw.text: Who eats whom: simple food chains

explain.say: Plants use the sun's energy to make their own food. These plants are called producers. They are the start of most food chains.
Animals that only eat plants are called plant eaters. We call them herbivores. A rabbit eating grass is a good example.
Animals that eat other animals are called meat eaters. We call them carnivores. A lion hunting a zebra is a clear example.
When you see a bunny munching on clover, the clover is the producer. The bunny eats the clover, so it is the herbivore. This shows the energy moving from plant to animal.
A common mistake is thinking that all animals eat everything. Remember that animals have specific diets. Herbivores only eat plants, and carnivores eat meat.

faq.q: Why do food chains always start with the sun?
faq.a: The sun provides the energy that makes plants grow. Plants use this energy to create food for everyone else. It is the original source of energy.
asks: Where does the energy come from?

faq.a: Yes, most plants are producers because they use sunlight to make their own food. This process is called photosynthesis. They create energy for the food chain.
asks: Do plants make their own food?

faq.q: What is the difference between a plant eater and a meat eater?
faq.a: Plant eaters only eat plants, like rabbits eating grass. Meat eaters only eat other animals, like lions eating meat. They eat different things.

faq.q: Can an animal eat both plants and meat?
faq.a: Yes, some animals eat both plants and meat. These animals are called omnivores. They have a varied diet.
asks: What if an animal eats everything?
Is there a middle group of eaters?

faq.q: Do food chains have to be very long?
faq.a: No, food chains can be short or long. They just show one path of energy moving from one living thing to another. The path can be simple.
asks: How long can a food chain be?

facts: The sun is the main source of energy.
Plants use sunlight to make food.
Meat eaters eat only other animals.

quiz.say: Which group starts the energy in a food chain?
quiz.why: Plants are producers and use the sun's energy to make food first.

wrong.0: Meat eaters need food from other animals, not the sun.
wrong.1: The sun gives energy, but plants are the ones that use it to make food.
wrong.2: Rabbits are consumers; they eat what the plants make.

quiz.say: A lion eating a zebra shows what type of food chain link?
quiz.why: The lion only eats other animals, which makes it a meat eater.

wrong.0: Producers are the things that make their own food.
wrong.1: The sun is the energy source, not the eater in the chain.
wrong.3: Plant eaters only eat things that grow from the ground.

quiz.say: If a fox eats berries and then eats a mouse, what is the fox?
quiz.why: The fox eats both plants (berries) and animals (mouse), so it is an omnivore.

wrong.0: This is wrong because the fox must eat other things to get energy.
wrong.2: This is wrong because the fox also eats the mouse, which is meat.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the fox also eats the berries, which are plants.
